questions.stem: Pointing to a photograph, Ravi says, 'She is the daughter of the only son of my grandfather.' How is the woman in the photograph related to Ravi?

options.option_text: Mother (grandfather's only son is Ravi's father; father's daughter is Ravi's sister, not mother)
Sister (correct: grandfather's only son = Ravi's father; father's daughter = Ravi's sister ✓)
Niece (Ravi's niece would be his brother's/sister's daughter, not his sister)
Cousin (she is the daughter of grandfather's only son=Ravi's father, so she is Ravi's sister, not cousin)

questions.explanation: B is correct. Grandfather's only son = Ravi's father. Daughter of Ravi's father = Ravi's sister. Therefore the woman is Ravi's SISTER.

questions.stem: A is B's brother. C is A's mother. D is C's father. E is D's mother. How is A related to D?

options.option_text: Son (A's mother=C; C's father=D; A is C's son; C is D's daughter; so A is D's grandson, not son)
Grandson (correct: A→C(mother)→D(grandfather); A is D's grandson ✓)
Nephew (nephew=sibling's son; D is A's grandfather, so A is grandson)
Great-grandson (that would require one more generation: E is D's mother, so D is E's son; A=D's grandson, not great-grandson)

questions.explanation: B is correct. Chain: A's mother = C. C's father = D. Therefore D is A's maternal grandfather. A is D's GRANDSON. (E is D's mother, making A E's great-grandson — but the question asks A's relationship to D.)

questions.stem: A man introduces a woman as 'the wife of the brother of my mother.' How is the woman related to the man?

options.option_text: Aunt (correct: mother's brother=maternal uncle; uncle's wife=maternal aunt ✓)
Sister-in-law (sister-in-law=wife of the man's own brother, not mother's brother)
Cousin (cousin=uncle's/aunt's child; the woman is the uncle's wife, not child)
Mother (mother's brother's wife is aunt, not his mother)

questions.explanation: A is correct. Mother's brother = the man's maternal uncle. Uncle's wife = the man's maternal AUNT. This is the standard maternal aunt relationship.

questions.stem: Seema said to Priya, 'Your mother's husband's sister is my mother.' How is Seema related to Priya?

options.option_text: Sister (Priya's mother's husband=Priya's father; father's sister=Priya's aunt; aunt=Seema's mother means Priya is Seema's cousin, not sister)
Cousin (correct: Priya's father's sister is Seema's mother → Seema is Priya's cousin ✓)
Niece (Seema's mother is Priya's aunt; Seema is the niece of Priya's father, but Seema and Priya are cousins)
Aunt (Seema is Priya's peer/cousin generation, not aunt generation)

questions.explanation: B is correct. Step by step: Priya's mother's husband = Priya's father. Priya's father's sister = Priya's paternal aunt. This aunt is Seema's mother. So Seema's mother is Priya's aunt. Therefore Seema is Priya's COUSIN (daughter of Priya's aunt).

questions.stem: In a family, P is the father of Q. R is the son of S. T is the brother of P. Q is the sister of R. How is S related to T?

options.option_text: Brother (need to find gender of S: R is S's son; Q is P's daughter, Q is R's sister; P is T's brother; we need more info on S's gender)
Sister-in-law (S is mother of R; R and Q are siblings; P is Q's father and T's brother; so S is P's wife; T is P's brother; S is T's sister-in-law ✓)
Aunt (aunt is of previous generation, not peer generation)
Mother (S is T's sister-in-law, not mother)

questions.explanation: B is correct. Q is sister of R → Q and R are siblings. P is Q's father → P is also R's father. R is S's son → S is R's mother → S is Q's mother → S is P's wife (since P is father). T is P's brother. Therefore S is the wife of P, who is T's brother → S is T's SISTER-IN-LAW.

questions.stem: Pointing to a boy, a girl says, 'He is the son of my mother's only brother.' The boy is related to the girl as her:

options.option_text: Brother (brother's son would be nephew; the boy is the girl's maternal uncle's son = cousin)
Cousin (correct: girl's mother's only brother=maternal uncle; uncle's son=cousin ✓)
Nephew (nephew=girl's sibling's son; the boy is uncle's son, making him cousin)
Uncle (uncle is one generation above; the boy is son of uncle = same generation as girl = cousin)

questions.explanation: B is correct. Mother's only brother = maternal uncle. Uncle's son = the girl's COUSIN (specifically, maternal cousin). This is one of the most straightforward blood relation patterns.

questions.stem: If A is the brother of B; B is the sister of C; C is the father of D, how is D related to A?

options.option_text: Nephew or niece (correct: C is D's father; C is B's brother; B is A's sister; C and A are siblings — wait: A is brother of B; B is sister of C means B and C are siblings; A,B,C are siblings; C is father of D; D is A's nephew or niece ✓)
Cousin (D is the child of A's sibling C, which makes D A's nephew/niece, not cousin)
Son or daughter (D is A's nephew/niece because D's parent C is A's sibling)
Grandchild (D is one generation below A's sibling C — that's nephew/niece, not grandchild)

questions.explanation: A is correct. A is B's brother; B is C's sister → A, B, C are all siblings. C is D's father. So D's parent (C) is A's sibling → D is A's NEPHEW or NIECE (depending on D's gender). Child of your sibling = nephew (if male) or niece (if female).

questions.stem: A woman says, 'The man in the photo is the only son of the father of my brother.' Who is the man in the photo?

options.option_text: Her father (father of her brother = her own father; only son of her father = her brother, not her father)
Her brother (correct: father of her brother = her father; only son of her father = her brother ✓)
Her son (son of her own father is her sibling, not her son)
Her grandfather (grandfather is two generations up; this is same generation)

questions.explanation: B is correct. 'Father of my brother' = her own father (same father). 'Only son of my father' = her brother (the sole male child). The man in the photo is her BROTHER.

questions.stem: In a family of 6 persons — A, B, C, D, E and F — there are two married couples. D is the grandmother of A and is a housewife. F is the grandfather of B and is retired. C is the son of F. E is the daughter of A's mother. If B is the brother of A, how many male members are there in the family?

options.option_text: 2 (too few — F and C are confirmed males, and B)
3 (correct: F=grandfather(M), C=son of F(M), B=A's brother(M); A,D,E=female; 3 males ✓)
4 (only 3 are clearly male)
2 (see above)

questions.explanation: B is correct. F = grandfather (male). C = F's son (male). B = A's brother (male). D = grandmother (female). A = child (gender from context: E is daughter of A's mother, and B is A's brother → A could be female). So: Males: F, C, B (3). Females: D (grandmother), E (daughter), A (sibling of B with female A implied by context). Total 3 males in the family.

questions.stem: Introducing a man, a woman says, 'His mother is the only daughter of my mother.' How is the man related to the woman?

options.option_text: Nephew (correct: 'only daughter of my mother' = the woman herself; so the man's mother is the woman; the man is the woman's SON ← wait: NEPHEW = sibling's son; SON = own son)
Son (correct: only daughter of my mother = the woman herself; so the man's mother is the woman → the man is her SON ✓)
Brother (man is same generation as woman? No — he is her son)
Cousin (cousin=same generation, different parents; he is her son)

questions.explanation: B is correct. 'My mother's only daughter' = the woman herself (if she is the only daughter). So the man's mother IS the woman introducing him. The man is the woman's own SON. This is a classic self-referential blood relation trick — 'only daughter of my mother' = the speaker herself.
